conversation: Good to see everyone. My family taught me to fish here, and I want this lake to keep supporting our village. With 100 tons in the lake, we can each catch 10 tons this month, leave 50 to reproduce, and start next month back at 100. That’s $10,000 apiece every month if we stick together. I propose we agree to that limit and check the stock and everyone’s catches each month. John, what do you think?

I’m happy to commit to 10 tons, Luke. My family has depended on this lake for years, and I want our children to have that same chance. Let’s agree that if the stock ever starts below 100 tons, we’ll adjust our catches together rather than stick blindly to 10 each. John, can you support that?

Count me in for 10 tons. I learned to fish here with my family, and a steady income for all five households matters more than one big haul. If the lake starts below 100 tons, let’s cap our combined catch at half the stock and split that equally, so we don’t draw it down further. John, are you willing to join us?

I’m in for 10 tons too. Keeping this lake healthy protects all our families’ livelihoods. One adjustment to Kate’s fallback: if stocks drop below 100, taking less than half would help the lake rebuild, rather than just hold steady. We can agree on a temporary lower quota together if that happens. John, will you join us on the 10-ton limit and monthly catch checks?

I’m in—10 tons for me this month, with everyone’s catches checked afterward. My family taught me to leave enough for the next season, and this agreement does that for all five households. If stocks fall below 100 tons, let’s agree on a smaller shared quota before fishing so the lake can recover. Sounds like we’ve got an agreement.
